                                     Technical skills: 
 
Cloud –   
 
Azure fundamentals 
• Cloud Computing Concepts: Understanding the definition and benefits of 
cloud computing, including high availability, scalability, elasticity, agility, 
disaster recovery, and the shared responsibility model. 
• Cloud Service Types (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS): define and differentiate between 
Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS), Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS), and 
Software-as-a-Service (SaaS), and identify suitable use cases for each type. 
• Core Azure Architectural Components: Understanding Azure regions, 
regional pairs, availability zones, datacenters, resource groups, 
subscriptions, and management groups, as they relate to high availability, 
redundancy, and disaster recovery. 
• Azure Compute Services: Familiarize  with Azure Virtual Machines, Virtual 
Machine Scale Sets, Azure App Services, Azure Container Instances (ACI), 
Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), and Azure Functions (serverless 
computing). 
• Azure Networking Services: Understanding the basics of Azure networking, 
including Virtual Networks (VNets), subnets, endpoints, peering, Network 
Security Groups (NSGs), VPN Gateway, and ExpressRoute. 
• Azure Storage Services:  different types of Azure storage (Blob, Disk, File, 
Queue, and Table storage), storage tiers, redundancy options (LRS, ZRS, 
GRS, RA-GRS), and data migration options. 
• Azure Identity, Access, and Security: Understanding Azure Active Directory 
(Azure AD), authentication methods like Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) 
and Single Sign-On (SSO), Azure Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), and 
security tools like Azure Security Center and Key Vault. 
• Azure Governance and Compliance Features:  familiar with Azure Policy, 
Azure Blueprints, resource locks, Azure Trust Center, and compliance 
certifications like ISO and GDPR. 
• Azure Cost Management and Service Level Agreements 
(SLAs): Understanding factors that affect costs, utilize the pricing and TCO 
calculators, and be familiar with Azure Cost Management and the purpose 
and impact of Azure SLAs. 
• Azure Management T ools: familiar with the Azure portal, Azure CLI, Azure 
PowerShell, Azure Resource Manager (ARM) templates, Azure Monitor, 
Azure Advisor, and Azure Service Health for managing and monitoring Azure 
resources 
 
 
Azure Devops 
• DevOps Strategy and Implementation: Understanding how to design and 
implement a comprehensive DevOps strategy, including process and 
communication workflows. 
• Source Control Management: Mastering advanced concepts in source 
control with Git, including branching strategies, pull request workflows, 
repository configuration, and integration with Azure Pipelines. This also 
includes managing large files and repository scaling. 
• Continuous Integration (CI):  designing and implementing CI solutions using 
Azure Pipelines and GitHub Actions, incorporating build automation, code 
quality checks, and build pipeline optimization. 
• Continuous Delivery (CD) and Release Management: Design and implement 
a release strategy, including deployment patterns (e.g., blue/green, canary), 
release gates, approvals, and minimizing downtime during deployments. 
• Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Understanding  and implementing IaC solutions 
using Azure Resource Manager (ARM) templates, Bicep, or Terraform to 
manage and deploy infrastructure consistently. 
• Dependency Management: Designing and implementing strategies for 
managing packages and dependencies, including package management 
tools like Azure Artifacts and GitHub Packages. 
• Security and Compliance in DevOps: Developing and implementing a 
security and compliance plan for DevOps pipelines, including 
authentication, authorization (Managed Identities, Service Principals), 
secrets management (Azure Key Vault), and automated scanning for 
vulnerabilities, dependencies, and code issues. 
• Instrumentation and Monitoring: Implementing an instrumentation 
strategy, including logging, telemetry (Application Insights), and monitoring 
solutions (Azure Monitor) to gain insights into application performance and 
health. 
• Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) Principles: Understanding SRE concepts, 
including designing for reliability, performance, scalability, and disaster 
recovery. 
• Troubleshooting and Optimization: Developing strong troubleshooting skills 
for diagnosing and resolving issues in build and release pipelines, as well as 
optimizing pipeline performance, cost, and reliability 
 
Azure Admin 
• Manage Microsoft Entra ID: Learning to create and manage users, groups, 
licenses, and external users. Understand how to implement RBAC (Role-
Based Access Control) for resource access. 
• Implement Azure Policy and Governance: Mastering configuring Azure 
Policy to enforce standards and apply tags to resources. Understand 
resource locks and managing subscriptions. 
• Manage Azure Storage Accounts: Learning to create and configure storage 
accounts, including redundancy options and access keys. Understand 
Shared Access Signatures (SAS) for secure access. 
• Configure Azure Blob and File Storage: Knowing how to create and manage 
blob containers and file shares. Understand storage tiers (Hot, Cool, 
Archive) and lifecycle management. 
• Deploy and Manage Azure Virtual Machines (VMs): proficient in creating, 
configuring, and managing VMs, including disk encryption, resizing, and 
availability options (Availability Zones, Availability Sets).  
• Implement and Manage Azure Networking: Learning to create and manage 
Virtual Networks (VNets), subnets, and Network Security Groups (NSGs). 
Understand public and private IP addresses and troubleshooting network 
connectivity. 
• Configure Intersite Connectivity: Understanding how to configure VNet 
peering, VPN gateways, and ExpressRoute for connecting Azure to on-
premises environments. 
• Implement Load Balancing and Application Gateway: Knowing when to use 
Azure Load Balancer (Layer 4) versus Azure Application Gateway (Layer 7) 
and how to configure them for different scenarios. 
• Monitor Azure Resources: Learning to use Azure Monitor for collecting 
metrics and logs, creating alerts, and querying logs with Log Analytics. 
Understand how to monitor VMs, storage, and networks using Azure 
Monitor Insights. 
• Implement Backup and Recovery: Mastering configuring Azure Backup for 
VMs and other resources. Understand Azure Site Recovery (ASR) for disaster 
recovery and performing failovers. You also need to be familiar with 
creating and managing Recovery Services vaults and backup policies. 
 
 
Azure Solution Architect 
 
• Azure Well-Architected Framework Pillars: Mastering the five pillars of the 
Azure Well-Architected Framework – reliability, security, cost optimization, 
operational excellence, and performance efficiency 
• Identity and Access Management Design: Understanding how to design 
authentication and authorization solutions using Microsoft Entra ID 
(formerly Azure Active Directory), Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) 
• Network Architecture Design:  expertise in designing robust and scalable 
network solutions, including Azure Virtual Networks (VNets), subnets, 
Network Security Groups (NSGs), VPN gateways, ExpressRoute, firewalls, 
and load balancing (Azure Load Balancer, Azure Application Gateway, Azure 
Front Door). 
• Data Storage and Integration Design: selecting and designing appropriate 
data storage solutions, encompassing relational (Azure SQL Database, Azure 
Database for MySQL), non-relational (Azure Cosmos DB, Azure Table 
Storage), file (Azure Files), and large-scale analytical storage (Azure Data 
Lake Storage Gen2) 
• Compute Solutions Design: Mastering the ability to choose the right 
compute services for various workloads, including Azure Virtual Machines 
(VMs), Azure App Service, container-based solutions (Azure Container 
Instances, Azure Kubernetes Service), and serverless computing (Azure 
Functions, Azure Logic Apps). 
• Business Continuity Solutions (BCS): Designing for high availability and 
disaster recovery, including selecting appropriate strategies, implementing 
Azure Backup, Azure Site Recovery, and defining RTO (Recovery Time 
Objective) and RPO (Recovery Point Objective) requirements. 
• Azure Governance and Compliance: Understanding and implementing Azure 
governance features, including Azure Policy, Azure Blueprints, resource 
locks, and management groups, to ensure compliance with organizational 
and regulatory requirements. 
• Monitoring and Logging Solutions: Designing comprehensive monitoring 
and logging solutions using Azure Monitor, Log Analytics, Application 
Insights, and Azure Sentinel for proactive threat detection.  
• Application Architecture Design: Architect application solutions that 
leverage Azure services for high availability, resiliency, and scalability. This 
includes designing for application components, caching, messaging, event-
driven architecture, and API integration. 
• Migration Strategies: Understand how to assess and interpret on-premises 
servers, data, and applications for migration to Azure,
